content.comment_body: Hello, I've configured communication between [product_name] and [product_name] [version_no]. Data transfer works as expected—I can read and write data from [product_name] to the database in [product_name]. However, when I disconnect the Ethernet cable from [product_name] and reconnect it, [product_name] doesn't automatically resume communication until I also unplug and replug its Ethernet cable. Does anyone know how to enable automatic communication restoration once the connection is re-established between these two devices? Thank you in advance.

Which device acts as the server and which as the client in your setup? In my case, I have a connection where [product_name] is the client and [product_name] [version_no] is the server. If I disconnect and reconnect the Ethernet cable on either device, the connection resumes immediately.

I've tried a second test with the roles reversed: now [product_name] is the server and [product_name] [version_no] is the client. In this case, if the Ethernet cable is disconnected and reconnected on either end, the connection doesn't automatically re-establish. Only a cold reboot of [product_name] [version_no] restores communication.

Hi, With [product_name] [version_no] as the server and [product_name] as the client, I've repeated the test multiple times. Sometimes communication resumes automatically after reconnecting [product_name] [version_no], but more often it doesn't resume until I reconnect the [product_name]'s Ethernet cable. On one occasion, nothing restored communication until I reloaded the program in [product_name]. Possibly restarting [product_name] [version_no] would have helped, but I didn't try. The LED on [product_name] flashes as if it's communicating, but it doesn't read or write data to the database.
From my experience, my setup behaves as described in my first response and doesn't face these issues.

Okay, I notice that there is a difference between your screenshot and mine. In your connection window, you see the link between [product_name] and [product_name]. In my connection window, I only see [product_name] with the connection ending below it. I'll try adding a [product_name] device so I can draw the connection between the two, and see if that changes anything.

I simply created a network project with [product_name] and a [product_name] [version_no] compatible device. I drew the connection with the cursor, starting from [product_name], which sets [product_name] as the client.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing unreliable automatic reconnection between [product_name] and [product_name] [version_no] after Ethernet disruptions. Sometimes communication resumes on its own, other times manual actions such as unplugging and replugging cables, restarting devices, or reloading programs are required. Differences in network setup and device roles contribute to inconsistent behavior and confusion among users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the system to automatically restore connectivity between [product_name] and [product_name] [version_no] when the Ethernet cable is reconnected, with no need for manual actions or program reloads.
